svg.desc: Banner for a paper on when the closed-form Gaussian answer for Gromov–Wasserstein transport is exact. Two discs show the same cloud of points from a standard Gaussian distribution in the plane, each with a line below it standing for a standard Gaussian on a line. In the left disc, straight vertical blue lines mark the points that a straight projection sends to the same place on the line; this is the best Gaussian pairing and has objective 12. In the right disc, orange curves bend inwards away from the middle: they are exact level sets of the paper's Gaussian-preserving flow at time one seventh, which keeps the line exactly standard Gaussian and provably scores below 76/7, about 10.86 (about 10.47 numerically). On the right, a number line from 8 to 12 marks 12 for projection, 76/7 for the curved pairing, and a green band from 8.68 to 10.85 where the true optimum is proved to lie. A footnote says the Gaussian shortcut is exact if and only if the two spectra are proportional, and is never off by more than a factor of two.
svg.text: Plane to line: the closed-form Gaussian answer is not the optimum
Points on one coloured curve are sent to the same point of the line; both pairings keep the line exactly N(0, 1)
GW objective for plane → line (lower is better)
Gaussian shortcut exact iff spectra proportional; never off by more than a factor of two
